newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 16.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - A new concept for a policy to support exports, which the Industry and Trade Ministry is preparing, should not put heavy demands on government finances. A decision on the programme should be made by the end of October.

- There was no strong reaction to the central bank's decision to decrease its repo rate to 29 percent and announcing that this week it will open access for foreign investors to the local money market.
- Nova Hut Ostrava had net profit of 254 million crowns last year on turnover of 23.2 billion crowns. Shareholders decided on Friday not to pay a 1996 dividend.
- Last year, Skoda Liaz posted a loss of 380 million crowns, nearly treble its losses in 1995. Liaz had revenue of 2.22 billion crowns after selling 989 vehicles, although it sold 762 in 1995.
- From today, Jihocesky Pivovar is increasing its prices on average by 60 to 80 crowns per hectolitre.

- Czech Railways had record losses last year of 4.7 billion crowns, 1.7 billion more than in 1995. Losses in passenger transport increased to 8.2 billion from 6.5, while profits in freight transport decreased to 1.9 from 2.8 billion crowns.

- The cabinet should decide in the near future on a method of privatising three brown coal mining companies -- Mostecke Uhelny, Severoceske Doly Chomutov and Sokolovske Uhelny, in which the state owns 46.3, 55 and 48.7 percent stakes respectively. The stakes are worth more than 13 billion crowns.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Finance Minister Ivan Pilip has decided to ignore the law for a few days in order to pay thousands of state workers their delayed wages.
- President Vaclav Havel's office will be affected the most by prepared budget cuts. Only 77.2 percent of the office's original budget remains after the cuts.
- According to the chairman of the Czech National Bank, privatisation of most strategic companies, including large domestic banks, should be finished within one to two years.

- During the first four months of this year, Prvni Investicni funds were profitable. Rentiersky IF had profits of 89.5 million, IF Bohatstvi 62.3 million, Kristalovy IF 11.8 million, IF Obchod 44.3 million and IF Energetika 1.4 million.

PRAVO - According to Finance Minister Ivan Pilip, the cabinet should discuss material for beginning privatisation of Komercni Banka and CSOB this Wednesday. These two banks should be privatised in the second half of the year, and Ceska Sporitelna should follow next year.
- Chairman of Parliament and leader of the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD), Milos Zeman, said Finance Minister Ivan Pilip is the most foolish minister in the cabinet.
- During the 55th anniversary of the destruction of the town Lidice, President Vaclav Havel warned against underestimating racial hatred for foreigners and minorities.

- Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl said after meeting with his South African counterpart Alec Erwin that trade with South Africa does not coincide with the economic potential of both countries. For the first four months of this year, the trade deficit with this country was $4.8 million.

LIDOVE NOVINY - From today, Komercni Banka will decrease rates on newly established seven-day accounts with a fixed interest rate in all three bands by three percentage points to between 12 and 23 percent.

- President Vaclav Havel said the voice of the United States for its support of the Czech Republic's entry into NATO is very strong, and he thinks it is nearly certain that the Czech Republic will be accepted.
- Deputy Prime Minister and the chairman of the Christian Democrats, Josef Lux, said disputes within the coalition have been and will be.
- The chairman of the opposition Social Democrats, Milos Zeman, announced yesterday that his party will propose to regulate the prices of medicines.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
